2607.28347.title: LLMs struggle to simulate human belief updates in controlled environments
2607.28347.paper_summary: LLMs are increasingly deployed as proxies for human study participants in social science experiments, yet the fidelity of this practice has rarely been tested directly. We test whether six LLMs can simulate individual human belief updates, comparing LLM outputs 1-to-1 against ground truth data from 391 UK participants on Prolific, who updated their stances on three discussion topics after reading Reddit comments. Each participant was simulated by an LLM conditioned on a persona derived from their demographic and personality trait data. We find that some LLMs (Qwen3-32B and GPT-5-Mini) can match the human post-stance distribution, but only when given participants' actual initial stances. All six models fail to simulate initial stances themselves and to produce faithful belief updates from self-generated stances. Three systematic biases emerge across all models: overrepresentation of neutral positions, more frequent but smaller belief shifts than humans, and a failure to rank comments by convincingness. Demographic and personality trait personas had no consistent effect on fidelity. LLM simulations of human belief dynamics are only reliable when grounded in realistic starting conditions, that current multi-round social media simulations rarely provide.
2607.28347.paper_summary_zh: LLMs 正在社會科學實驗中越來越多地被用作人類研究參與者的代理，但這種做法的真實性很少被直接測試。我們測試了六個 LLM 是否能夠模擬個體人類信念的更新，將 LLM 的輸出與來自 391 名英國參與者的真實數據進行 1 對 1 的比較，這些參與者在閱讀 Reddit 評論後更新了他們對三個討論主題的立場。每位參與者都由 LLM 模擬，並根據他們的人口統計和人格特徵數據衍生出的人物設定進行調整。我們發現某些 LLM（Qwen3-32B 和 GPT-5-Mini）能夠匹配人類的後立場分佈，但僅在提供參與者的實際初始立場時。所有六個模型都無法模擬初始立場，並且無法從自生成的立場中產生忠實的信念更新。所有模型中出現了三種系統性偏見：中立立場的過度代表性、比人類更頻繁但更小的信念變化，以及未能根據說服力對評論進行排序。人口統計和人格特徵的人物設定對真實性沒有一致的影響。當 LLM 模擬人類信念動態時，只有在基於現實的起始條件下才可靠，而當前的多輪社交媒體模擬很少提供這樣的條件。
